mainTopic: Visiting the sick on שבת, and the ban on reading or checking things by lamplight on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about what to say when visiting a sick person on שבת. The גמרא rules that רבי חנינא's practice, including the patient 'among the sick of ישראל,' follows רבי יוסי. It then explains why רבי אלעזר could bless the sick in Aramaic: the שכינה is with the sick person, as the verse 'ה׳ יסעדנו על ערש דוי' shows. Next, the גמרא returns to the משנה's ban on reading by lamplight on שבת. The ban applies no matter how high the lamp is. Two people may read together only if they study the same subject, and around a bonfire even ten people may not. רבא allows an אדם חשוב to read, and the story of רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע is shown to be a special case. The גמרא then settles two ברייתות about a שמש checking dishes by lamplight, and records רב and רבי ירמיה בר אבא on the mixed case. Finally, it explains that the משנה's חזן may only glance to arrange the beginnings of his sections, and the question about reading the whole section continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's wording for blessing a sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the visitor should bless the sick person and also all the sick of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'May the Omnipresent have compassion on you and on the sick of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about what a visitor says to a sick person on שבת. Here רבי יהודה gives his version of the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's wording has two parts: a blessing for this patient ('on you') and a separate blessing for all other sick people ('and on the sick of ישראל'). The patient is mentioned first, on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Place,' meaning the Omnipresent, a name for God

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'May the Omnipresent have compassion upon you
and upon the sick of Israel.'
phrases.notes: The patient and the other sick people are listed as two separate groups.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began on the previous amud, listing opinions on what to say to a sick person on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say: 'May God have compassion on you and on the sick of ישראל.'

steps.title: רבי יוסי's wording: the patient among all the sick
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the blessing should place the sick person inside the group of all the sick of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: 'May the Omnipresent have compassion on you among the sick of ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a slightly different wording. He blesses the patient as one member of the whole community of sick people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is one word: רבי יהודה says 'and on' (וְעַל), while רבי יוסי says 'among' (בְּתוֹךְ). For רבי יוסי, the patient is blessed together with everyone else, which joins his prayer to the merit of the community.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions mention all the sick of ישראל. The only difference is whether the patient is listed separately ('and on') or included inside the group ('among'). Watch that one word.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
'May the Omnipresent have compassion upon you
among the sick of Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative wording that disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say: 'May God have compassion on you among the sick of ישראל.'

steps.title: שבנא איש ירושלים's custom when visiting the sick
steps.stepSummary: שבנא of ירושלים said 'שלום' when he came in, and a longer שבת-appropriate blessing when he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: שבנא of ירושלים, when he entered, would say 'שלום.' When he left he would say: 'It is שבת, when one may not cry out. Healing is soon to come, His compassion is great, and rest in peace on שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reports the personal practice of a man named שבנא from ירושלים when visiting the sick on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His farewell avoids crying out in prayer, since שבת is not a time for pleading. Instead it comforts the patient: healing is near, God's mercy is great, so rest peacefully on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And rest in peace (enjoy שבת calmly)

phrases.english: Shevna, a man of Jerusalem,
upon his entering would say: 'Shalom,'
and upon his leaving would say:
'It is Shabbat, when one refrains from crying out,
and healing is soon to come,
and His compassion is abundant,
and rest in peace.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more practice to the ברייתא's list of what to say.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Greet with 'שלום' on entering, and on leaving give a calming שבת blessing that does not plead.

steps.title: Whose view does רבי חנינא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches רבי חנינא's rule that you must include your sick relative among all the sick of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what רבי חנינא said: someone who has a sick person in his house must include him among the sick of ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a later rule from רבי חנינא and asks which side of the ברייתא it fits. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's word 'include' (שֶׁיְּעָרְבֶנּוּ) is the clue. The question is meant to link his rule to the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does it go? (Whose view does it follow?)

phrases.english: According to whom is this
that Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חוֹלֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
phrases.english: one who has a sick person in his house
must include him among the sick of Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects a later אמורא's rule to the תנאים dispute just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's wording is the basis for רבי חנינא's rule.

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא's rule follows רבי יוסי, who said 'among the sick of ישראל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רבי חנינא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's word 'among' (בְּתוֹךְ) is exactly the 'including' that רבי חנינא requires. The practical outcome is that we pray for a sick person as part of the whole community.
steps.whatToRemember: When praying for a sick person, include him 'among the sick of ישראל' (רבי יוסי, as רבי חנינא rules). This is the source of the familiar wording 'בתוך שאר חולי ישראל.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the standard wording still used today in the מי שברך for the sick.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חנינא's rule follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Visiting the sick and comforting mourners on שבת was permitted reluctantly
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the חכמים only permitted comforting mourners and visiting the sick on שבת with difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: Only with difficulty did they permit comforting mourners and visiting the sick on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching of רבי חנינא: these two מצוות were allowed on שבת only reluctantly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both visits bring sadness, and sadness clashes with the joy of שבת. The חכמים still allowed them because of the importance of the מצוה, but only barely.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:
With difficulty they permitted
comforting mourners and visiting the sick on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching from the same אמורא on the same topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Visiting the sick and comforting mourners on שבת is permitted, but only reluctantly.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר blessed the sick sometimes in Hebrew, sometimes in Aramaic
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports that רבי אלעזר sometimes blessed a sick person in Hebrew and sometimes in Aramaic.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: When we would go with רבי אלעזר to ask after a sick person, sometimes he said: 'May the Omnipresent remember you for peace,' and sometimes he said to him: 'May the Merciful One remember you for peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: A story about how רבי אלעזר blessed the sick. He used the same blessing in two languages. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version is Hebrew; the second (רַחֲמָנָא יִדְכְּרִינָךְ לִשְׁלָם) is the same meaning in Aramaic. Using Aramaic for a prayer is what the גמרא will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person (literally: one who is swollen)
May He remember you for peace (Hebrew)
May the Merciful One remember you for peace (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָזְלִינַן בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: When we would go after Rabbi Elazar
to inquire after a sick person,
sometimes he said: 'May the Omnipresent remember you for peace.'
phrases.notes: This version of the blessing is in Hebrew.

phrases.english: And sometimes he said to him:
'May the Merciful One remember you for peace.'
phrases.notes: Aramaic, said perhaps for a patient who did not understand Hebrew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of the blessing to the language of the blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר blessed the sick in both Hebrew and Aramaic.

steps.title: Challenge: one may not pray for one's needs in Aramaic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's use of Aramaic, citing רב יהודה and רבי יוחנן that angels do not take up Aramaic prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he do this? Didn't רב יהודה say: A person should never ask for his needs in Aramaic? And רבי יוחנן said: Whoever asks for his needs in Aramaic, the ministering angels do not attend to him, because the ministering angels do not recognize Aramaic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי אלעזר could pray in Aramaic, since two אמוראים teach that this does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן explains the problem: the angels carry prayers up to God, but they do not know Aramaic. So an Aramaic prayer, like רבי אלעזר's, would seem to go nowhere.

phrases.english: How could he do this?
But didn't Rav Yehuda say:
A person should never request
his needs in the Aramaic language.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who requests his needs in Aramaic —
the ministering angels do not attend to him,
because the ministering angels do not
recognize the Aramaic language!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the practice described in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's Aramaic blessing for the sick person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Prayers go up through angels, angels do not understand Aramaic, so an Aramaic prayer should be pointless and avoided.

steps.title: A sick person is different: the שכינה is with him
steps.stepSummary: A sick person is an exception because the שכינה is right there with him, so no angel is needed to carry the prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sick person is different, because the Divine Presence is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a sick person is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against Aramaic depends on needing angels as messengers. Next to a sick person the שכינה itself is present, so the prayer reaches God directly and any language works.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why one may pray for a sick person in any language when standing beside him.

phrases.english: A sick person is different,
for the Divine Presence is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: an exception to the general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every prayer in Aramaic fails because the angels cannot carry it.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a sick person the שכינה is present, so angels are not needed and Aramaic is fine.

steps.title: Source: God supports the sick person
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן quotes רב, who derives from a verse in Psalms that God supports the sick, backing up 'the שכינה is with him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ענן said in the name of רב: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא supports the sick person? As it says: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for its answer that the שכינה is with the sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says God Himself supports the sick person on his sickbed. That means God is present right there, which is exactly what the answer in step 9 needs.

phrases.english: As Rav Anan said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
supports the sick person?
As it is said: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the שכינה is with the sick person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Psalms 41:4, 'ה׳ יסעדנו על ערש דוי,' as taught by רב.

steps.title: ברייתא: how to sit when visiting the sick
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a visitor sits humbly below the patient because the שכינה is above the patient's head, supporting the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught so in a ברייתא: One who comes to visit a sick person should not sit on the bed or on a chair. Rather, he wraps himself and sits in front of him, because the שכינה is above the head of the sick person, as it says: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב's idea and adds a practical rule for visitors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שכינה rests above the patient's head, the visitor must not sit up high. He wraps himself respectfully and sits low before the patient. The ברייתא uses the same verse.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical guideline in the laws of visiting the sick: sit humbly and do not sit higher than the patient's head.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
One who enters to visit the sick person

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֵשֵׁב לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי מִטָּה
phrases.english: should sit neither on the bed
nor on a chair,
rather he wraps himself and sits before him,
because the Divine Presence is above
the head of the sick person,
as it is said: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא that supports רב's teaching in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That the שכינה is present with the sick person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how a visitor sits, based on the same verse.

steps.title: God feeds the sick person
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רבין, who reads the same verse to teach that God feeds the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said in the name of רבין: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא feeds the sick person? As it says: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching on the same verse, this time showing that God also nourishes the sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין reads יִסְעָדֶנּוּ as 'sustain with food' (as in סְעוּדָה, a meal). This adds to God's closeness to the sick person.

keyTerms.meaning: Will support/sustain him (related to סְעוּדָה, a meal)

steps.whatToRemember: The verse 'ה׳ יסעדנו על ערש דוי' teaches that God is with the sick person. That is why one may pray for him in Aramaic, why a visitor sits humbly before him, and that God sustains him.

phrases.english: And Rava said in the name of Ravin:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He,
feeds the sick person?
As it is said: 'God will support him on the bed of illness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching from the same verse, closing this topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God feeds the sick, learned from יסעדנו.

steps.title: No reading by lamplight, however high the lamp
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה's rule against reading by lamplight on שבת. רבה says it applies even if the lamp is very high up.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one may not read by the light of the lamp.' רבה said: Even if it is two men's height high, even two ox-goads high, even ten houses stacked one on top of the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. רבה explains that the ban on reading by lamplight applies even when the lamp is far out of reach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the reader will tilt the lamp to get more light, which is forbidden on שבת. You might think a lamp that cannot be reached is safe. רבה says no: the חכמים made one general decree with no exceptions.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of the lamp
Ox-goads (long poles used for driving oxen or plowing)

steps.confusionAlert: Even a lamp that cannot possibly be reached is included. The decree does not depend on whether the reader can actually tilt it.

phrases.english: 'And one may not read by the light of the lamp.'
Rabba said:
Even if it is two statures high,
and even two ox-goads high,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ עֲשָׂרָה בָּתִּים זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה.
phrases.english: and even ten houses one atop the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יִקְרָא לְאוֹר הַנֵּר. אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of visiting the sick and returns to the משנה's laws about the lamp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading by lamplight on שבת is forbidden no matter how high the lamp is.

steps.title: Inference: one person may not read, but two may
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's singular wording, the גמרא infers that two people reading together may do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is one person who may not read, but two are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה's wording. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'he' may not read, which suggests one person alone. Two people can remind each other not to tilt the lamp, so they would be allowed.

phrases.english: It is one person who may not read,
but two — it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד הוּא דְּלָא לִיקְרֵי, הָא תְּרֵי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further inference from the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By inference from the משנה, two people reading together are permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא forbids even two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says neither one nor two may read by lamplight, which contradicts the inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: neither one nor two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference with a ברייתא that forbids even two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference allowed two readers, but the ברייתא openly forbids two. So the two sources seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: But it was taught: neither one nor two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that two people may read by lamplight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא forbids two, which contradicts what was inferred from the משנה.

steps.title: Same subject versus two different subjects
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר: two reading the same subject are allowed; two reading different subjects are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is not difficult. Here it is one subject; there it is two subjects.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the contradiction by explaining that each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both people study the same text, they pay attention to each other and will remind one another not to tilt the lamp, so it is permitted. If each studies something different, each is absorbed in his own text and will not notice, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
Here... there (each source refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Two people may read by lamplight on שבת only if they study the same subject together, so that they will remind each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: It is not difficult:
here, in one subject;
phrases.notes: Here it's allowed, because they can keep an eye on each other.

phrases.english: there, in two subjects.
phrases.notes: Here it's not allowed, because each one is absorbed in his own text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה (allowing two) and the ברייתא (forbidding two) contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two reading one subject together are permitted; two reading different subjects are forbidden.

steps.title: A bonfire is forbidden even for ten people
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: reading by the light of a bonfire is forbidden even for ten people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: And with a bonfire, even ten people are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds that around a bonfire, even a large group may not read by its light.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People around a bonfire sit spread out and do not watch each other. So the 'reminding' that protects two people reading together does not work, and anyone might stir the fire for more light.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִמְדוּרָה, אֲפִילּוּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם אָסוּר.
phrases.english: And with a bonfire, even ten people are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where a group reading together still does not help.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading by the light of a bonfire on שבת is forbidden even for ten people.

steps.title: An important person may read by lamplight
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an אדם חשוב may read by lamplight on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he is an important person, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to the rule against reading by lamplight. An important person is allowed to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban exists because a reader might tilt the lamp. An important person does not handle a greasy lamp himself, even on a weekday, so the worry does not apply to him. The rule still stands, and this is only an exception to how it applies.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he is an important person, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: He does not normally handle a dirty, oily lamp, so there is little fear that he will tilt it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם אָדָם חָשׁוּב הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit to the lamplight ban, after the cases of two readers and a bonfire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אדם חשוב may read by lamplight on שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from the story of רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how even the great רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע came to tilt the lamp, or nearly did. This challenges רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא challenges this: One may not read by lamplight, in case he tilts the lamp. רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע said, 'I will read and not tilt.' Once he read and wanted to tilt. He said, 'How great are the words of the Sages who said not to read by lamplight.' רבי נתן says he actually did tilt it. He wrote in his notebook: 'I, ישמעאל בן אלישע, read and tilted a lamp on שבת. When the בית המקדש is rebuilt, I will bring a fat חטאת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא with a story. A very important person, רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע, still came to tilt the lamp, or almost did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If importance protected a person, רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע, who was a כהן גדול, should have been safe. Yet he wanted to tilt the lamp, and according to רבי נתן he actually did. That suggests the ban applies to important people too.

keyTerms.meaning: in case he tilts the lamp
a fat sin-offering (brought for an accidental sin)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל did not sin on purpose. He tilted the lamp absent-mindedly, which is why he speaks of bringing a חטאת. A חטאת is only brought for an accidental sin.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִקְרָא לְאוֹר הַנֵּר, שֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה.
phrases.english: One may not read by the light of a lamp, lest he tilt it.
Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha said:
I will read and will not tilt.
Once he read and sought to tilt it.
He said: How great are the words of the Sages

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים לֹא יִקְרָא לְאוֹר הַנֵּר.
phrases.english: who would say one may not read by lamplight.
Rabbi Natan says: He read and did tilt it,
and he wrote in his notebook:
I, Yishmael ben Elisha,
read and tilted a lamp on Shabbat;
when the Temple will be rebuilt
I will bring a fat sin-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: לֹא יִקְרָא לְאוֹר הַנֵּר, שֶׁמָּא יַטֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's exception for an אדם חשוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an אדם חשוב may read by lamplight.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע was certainly an אדם חשוב, yet he came to tilt the lamp. So importance does not remove the worry.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל was unusually humble
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains that רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע is a special case because he acted like a simple person when it came to Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: רבי ישמעאל בן אלישע is different, since he treated himself like an ordinary person when it came to Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא defends רבא. He says the story does not disprove the rule, because רבי ישמעאל did not behave like a typical important person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exception depends on how the person actually behaves, not on his title. A normal important person keeps his distance from handling the lamp. רבי ישמעאל was humble in his learning and would adjust the lamp himself, so the worry did apply to him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha is different,
since he makes himself
with regard to words of Torah like a simple person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and keeps רבא's ruling in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the person in the story was unusual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any important person, including רבי ישמעאל, should be safe from tilting the lamp.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an important person who actually keeps his distance from handling lamps is exempt. רבי ישמעאל acted like a הדיוט, so the rule applied to him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: an אדם חשוב may read by lamplight. The story of רבי ישמעאל is no proof against this, because he humbly acted like a הדיוט.

steps.title: Two ברייתות clash about a servant checking cups
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא lets a שמש check cups and bowls by lamplight. Another forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: A servant may check cups and bowls by lamplight. Another ברייתא teaches: He may not check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two teachings that contradict each other about a servant checking dishes by lamplight. It is setting up an answer that will resolve them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking dishes for cleanliness is like reading: you look closely, and you might tilt the lamp for better light. The two ברייתות give opposite rulings on this, so the גמרא needs to find a difference between the cases.

phrases.english: It was taught in one baraita:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁמָּשׁ בּוֹדֵק כּוֹסוֹת וּקְעָרוֹת לְאוֹר הַנֵּר.
phrases.english: A servant may examine cups and bowls by lamplight.
And it was taught in another: He may not examine!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: שַׁמָּשׁ בּוֹדֵק כּוֹסוֹת וּקְעָרוֹת לְאוֹר הַנֵּר. וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: לֹא יִבְדּוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from reading to a related case of close examination by lamplight.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about a שמש checking dishes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One permits and the other forbids the same act, which is a direct contradiction.

steps.title: Permanent servant versus temporary servant
steps.stepSummary: A permanent servant may not check, but a temporary servant may.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: Here it means a permanent servant; there it means a servant who is not permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is about a different kind of servant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanent servant fears his master and checks very carefully, so he might tilt the lamp, and he is forbidden. A temporary servant is less worried and checks casually, so he is allowed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, with a regular servant;
phrases.notes: This one is forbidden, because he checks carefully.

phrases.english: there, with a servant who is not regular.
phrases.notes: This one is permitted, because he checks casually.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of servant (כאן... כאן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות speak about the same servant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permanent servant is forbidden and the temporary one is permitted.

steps.title: Second answer: oil lamp versus naphtha lamp
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות speak about a permanent servant. The difference is an oil lamp versus a naphtha lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you like, say: Both are about a permanent servant, and it is not difficult. This one is about an oil lamp, and that one is about a naphtha lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to resolve the contradiction. Here the difference is the type of lamp, not the type of servant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an oil lamp he might tilt it, so it is forbidden. Naphtha is foul-smelling and messy, so nobody touches that lamp, and it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
this and that are both with a regular servant,
and it is not difficult:
this is with an oil lamp, and that is with a naphtha lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא בְּשַׁמָּשׁ קָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of fuel.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference must be the type of servant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a permanent servant may check by a naphtha lamp, but not by an oil lamp.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not reject the first one. It is simply another way to resolve the contradiction. The next step asks about the case that mixes the two answers.

steps.title: What about a temporary servant with an oil lamp?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a temporary servant using an oil lamp, which falls between the two answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the rule for a servant who is not permanent, using an oil lamp?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that comes from combining the two answers. It is setting up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a temporary servant points toward permitting it, but the oil lamp points toward forbidding it. Which factor wins?

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked before them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
A servant who is not regular, with an oil lamp, what is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שַׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ קָבוּעַ בִּדְמִשְׁחָא מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a mixed case out of the two answers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a temporary servant may check dishes by an oil lamp.

steps.title: רב: permitted, but not taught publicly
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that it is permitted, but this is not publicly taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: That is the הלכה, but we do not instruct people that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the temporary servant may check by an oil lamp. However, a rabbi should not announce this as a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself permits it. Still, teaching it openly might lead people to be careless with lamps, so only someone who already knows may rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the law, but we do not rule that way publicly

phrases.english: Rav said:
It is the halacha, but we do not instruct so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה וְאֵין מוֹרִין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא: permitted and taught publicly
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא rules that it is permitted and may be taught publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: That is the הלכה, and we instruct people that way.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion goes further than רב. It is permitted, and a rabbi may openly rule this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the law. They disagree only on whether to teach it openly, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא sees no reason to hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: we instruct or issue a ruling

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
It is the halacha, and we instruct so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה וּמוֹרִין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב about teaching the ruling publicly.

steps.title: Story: רבי ירמיה's servant at רב אסי's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's servant checked cups by lamplight at רב אסי's house. רב אסי told his wife to let him be, since he follows his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא visited the house of רב אסי. His servant got up and checked the cups by the lamplight. רב אסי's wife said to him, 'But you, sir, do not do this?' He said to her, 'Leave him. He holds like his master.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רבי ירמיה בר אבא's opinion being practiced. Even רב אסי, who was stricter himself, accepted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servant was temporary in רב אסי's house, and he used an oil lamp, which is exactly the case in question. רב אסי did not do this himself, but he respected that the servant followed his own master's ruling.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אַסִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba happened to come to the house of Rav Asi.
His servant stood up
and was examining by the light of the lamp.
His wife said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי's wife speaking to רב אסי.

phrases.english: But the master does not do so?
He said to her: Leave him,
he holds like his master.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי ירמיה בר אבא's ruling being practiced.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's lenient ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of his servant at רב אסי's house.
steps.whatToRemember: A temporary servant using an oil lamp may check dishes. רב says this is not publicly taught, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא says it is.

steps.title: Back to the משנה about the attendant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'In truth they said, the חזן...'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In truth they said: the attendant...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to quote a line from the משנה. It is setting up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the חזן may look where the children are reading, but he himself should not read. The גמרא is about to point out a tension in that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: in truth they said (introduces an established rule)

phrases.english: In truth they said: the attendant, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the servant discussion back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חזן may look where the children are reading, but he may not read himself.

steps.title: Doesn't 'sees' mean reading?
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the משנה says the חזן 'sees,' which seems to mean reading. That clashes with the end of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said in the first part 'he sees.' Doesn't that mean to read?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה from its own wording. It seems to permit reading at the start and forbid it at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'רואה' means reading, the משנה contradicts itself. So the word needs a narrower meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: but you said in the first part

phrases.english: But you said in the first clause 'he sees.'
Is it not to read?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמְרַתְּ רֵישָׁא רוֹאֶה. מַאי לָאו, לִקְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה about the חזן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'sees' means reading, the start of the משנה permits what the end forbids.

steps.title: He only arranges the section openings
steps.stepSummary: 'Sees' means he looks only to find and arrange where his sections begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means to arrange the beginnings of his sections.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'seeing' is only a quick look to mark where each section starts. It is not real reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brief glance to locate the start of each portion is not close study, so there is less fear that he will tilt the lamp. Full reading stays forbidden.

phrases.english: No, to arrange the beginnings of his sections.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word ('רואה' means glancing, not reading).
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Sees' means only marking where the sections begin.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל also says the חזן may arrange the beginnings of his sections.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבה בר שמואל: But he may arrange the beginnings of his sections.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a matching statement from רבה בר שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא independently said the same thing, which confirms the reading of 'רואה' as arranging the section openings.

phrases.english: And so too Rabba bar Shmuel said:
But he may arrange the beginnings of his sections,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer just given.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that 'sees' means arranging the section openings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of רבה בר שמואל.

steps.title: And not the whole section?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether he really may not read the entire section.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the whole section, not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the limit just stated. This is a setup line, and the discussion continues on the next daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר שמואל allowed only the beginnings of the sections. The גמרא now asks whether reading the full section is really forbidden, which hints that a source may allow more.

phrases.english: And the entire section, not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the limit stated by רבה בר שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The limit that the חזן may arrange only the beginnings of the sections.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Is reading the whole section really forbidden? The answer continues on the next daf.
